observations: Photo shows a split AC outdoor unit (or a portable/indoor unit placed outdoors) with a large front grille and a white casing.
Brand text appears on the front label area, but it is not fully readable in this single photo.
A red/orange sticker with numbers appears on the right side of the front label area, but the capacity/model is not clearly readable.
No close-up of the rating plate (model/serial), no remote, and no power-on/working video is shown.
Seller says it is faulty, but the photo itself does not show the fault.

identity.kind: split AC (outdoor/indoor unit not fully confirmable from one photo)

claims.claim: Faulty inverter AC available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows an AC unit but does not show inverter status or the specific fault.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year.
claims.evidence: No receipt/date or warranty card is shown in the photo.

claims.claim: No fault at all, the motor was never opened.
claims.evidence: Seller’s own first line says it is faulty; the photo does not resolve which statement is true.

risks.risk: Actual fault type is unknown (e.g., compressor, fan motor, gas leak, PCB). Photos cannot confirm.
risks.proof: Short video of power-on with temperature/operation mode, plus a clear sound check (compressor start) and any error code on the display/remote.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / needs diagnosis and possible major repair.

risks.risk: Capacity (BTU) and exact model are not readable, which strongly affects Lagos pricing and repair cost.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rating plate showing model number and BTU/capacity (and serial).
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the worst-case assumption for an unknown-capacity AC (treated as lower-value/repairable unit).

risks.risk: Inverter vs non-inverter is not confirmable from the photo; inverter units price differently and repairs differ.
risks.proof: Photo of the label/plate where inverter is stated, or a clear shot of the control board/model marking.

risks.risk: Unit shown may be the outdoor unit or a different component; missing matching indoor/outdoor parts can make it unusable.
risks.proof: Photos of both indoor and outdoor units (if split), including the connecting pipes/ports and model plates for each.

risks.risk: Refrigerant leak or compressor failure may not be obvious until tested under load.
risks.proof: After power-on, show sustained cooling for at least 15–20 minutes (or show gauges/technician test if available).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as likely to require gas/compressor service.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the rating plate (model number, serial, BTU/capacity, inverter/non-inverter marking).
Video of the AC being powered on and running (compressor start + any error code).
If split: photos of both indoor and outdoor units with their rating plates.
Photos of the receipt and warranty card (showing date and model).
If the seller claims “motor never opened”: photo of the unit’s casing/fasteners to show it hasn’t been tampered with (and any service stickers).
response.reason: From the single photo, the AC’s exact model/capacity and the inverter status are not reliably readable, and the seller’s “faulty” vs “no fault” statements can’t be verified remotely. A power-on test and clear rating-plate close-up are needed before a safe price.
